prerequisites: Familiarity with script-type programming languages (e.g., Matlab, Python, JavaScript).
Proficiency in reading English is highly recommended.

learning_outcomes.text: Understand the value of data and the potential of analysis techniques for inspection, supervision, and improvement of industrial processes.
Know and apply techniques for preparing and adapting raw data for analysis.
Know and apply the most important feature extraction, modeling, and classification techniques for intelligent data analysis in industrial processes.
Know and apply dimensionality reduction techniques for visual representation of multivariate process data and for extracting high-value descriptive features.
Know and apply the basic principles of perception, interaction, and design for the development of efficient visualizations of knowledge and process data.
Know and apply the most important technologies for the development of visual analytics tools for process data.

syllabus_topics: Importing data. Common data sources and formats. Import methods and techniques.
Data curation. Filtering. Resampling. Handling missing data.
Data aggregation. Basic time aggregation using sliding windows.
Static features and descriptors (statistical, geometric, etc.).
Dynamic features and descriptors (frequency, wave parameters, etc.).
Aggregation based on more general grouping criteria.
Applications of regression algorithms and neural networks to estimation, system identification, and prediction in industrial processes.
Dimensionality reduction techniques. Applications in data and process state visualization.
Classification and clustering techniques. Applications for diagnosis and characterization of industrial processes.
Novelty detection techniques. Applications for fault detection and anomalous situations.
Fundamentals of perception and human visual system.
Design principles. Graphic excellence. Visual encoding of variables.
Technologies, languages, and software for data visualization.
Practical part: examples and case studies of the above techniques applied to the analysis of real or simulated data from engineering processes and systems.
assessment_rules: The final grade in the ordinary call is calculated as: Final Grade = 0.80 *T + 0.20 *P, where T is the grade obtained in the data analysis and visualization project and P is the grade obtained in written tests or evaluable tasks. No minimum grade is established for either component. In the extraordinary call, the same evaluable elements are used, and grades obtained in the ordinary call for written tests and tasks are retained. The project can be resubmitted to improve the grade.
